item.text: {"actions":[{"action":"Offer a numbered destination","mechanism":"A keyboard-operated position form moves an item directly to any final position from 1 through 40.","implementation":"Add a “Move” button opening a labeled numeric field and Apply/Cancel buttons. Define the entered number as the final position.","check":"Using only the keyboard, move item 37 to position 4; verify its position, then undo and verify the original order.","risk":"Reject invalid numbers without closing the form or changing order."},{"action":"Offer placement before or after another item","mechanism":"Choosing a neighboring title avoids requiring users to know the destination’s number.","implementation":"Provide native selectors for Before/After and destination item, excluding the moving item. Disambiguate duplicate titles with current positions; commit through shared move history.","check":"Place an item after a duplicate-titled destination using only the keyboard; verify the selected neighbor and successful undo.","risk":"Long title selectors need readable, unambiguous option labels."},{"action":"Provide one-step movement controls","mechanism":"Move up and Move down buttons support small adjustments without dragging or entering a destination.","implementation":"Expose native buttons in the focused item’s move panel. Keep focus on the activated control across updates; record each successful move separately.","check":"Move an item up three times using the keyboard, then undo three times; verify the exact starting order.","risk":"Boundary controls must explain unavailable moves without unexpectedly losing focus."},{"action":"Retain undo history until page closure","mechanism":"An ordered history preserves every committed reorder, rather than only the latest move or a temporary notification.","implementation":"Store immutable before/after ID sequences and a history cursor in page-lifetime state. Provide persistent Undo/Redo buttons; do not expire or cap undo entries.","check":"Perform 100 moves, navigate within the application, then undo every move without closing the page; verify the initial order.","risk":"A new move after undo should explicitly discard the redo branch."},{"action":"Reorder IDs without recreating items","mechanism":"Separating item records from their ordered ID sequence preserves identity through movement, undo, and rendering.","implementation":"Keep records keyed by existing IDs. Implement moves as remove-and-insert operations on the ID sequence; use those IDs as rendering keys.","check":"For every source/destination pair, verify unchanged ID membership and count; undo must restore the exact sequence and retain item-local state.","risk":"Regenerating IDs or using position-based keys can silently replace item state."},{"action":"Preserve focus and announce completed moves","mechanism":"Stable focus and concise status announcements make keyboard moves and reversals understandable without visual tracking.","implementation":"After applying or undoing, retain focus on the initiating control or restore it to the moved item’s button. Announce title and resulting position through a polite live region.","check":"With keyboard and screen reader, move and undo an item; confirm predictable focus and one accurate announcement per operation.","risk":"Avoid announcing the entire 40-item list after each change."}],"abstention_reason":""}
